newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, extending losses from Monday fueled by large movement of hogs held back by last week's winter storm, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to interior Iowa and southern Minnesota plants were seen ranging from $51.00 to $52.00. USDA Monday said the early top paid at plants Monday was $54.00, and later $53.00, which was $2.00 lower than midsession on Friday.
Illinois top prices at plants could range $52.50 to $53.00 and Indiana/Ohio top prices could span $51.00 to $51.50.
Producers started moving hogs Friday as plows unplugged country roads that had been blocked by wind-driven snow, dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Friday totalled 111,000 head, compared with USDA's earlier estimate for 105,000 and Saturday's was 38,000, compared with the estimate of 25,000, according to USDA.
Monday's estimated Iowa/southern Minnesota run was 120,000 head, USDA said.
